description: Repos with maintained release branches also set baseBranchPatterns, e.g. ["$default", "/^rel-/"].
Non-major updates are automerged once the required checks pass; major updates keep a PR for review.
Off by default in Renovate; without this, the hook revs pinned in .pre-commit-config.yaml never get update PRs.

poetry.description: We don't use Poetry, and its manager takes PEP 621 pyproject.toml files away from pep621.

customManagers.description: Update the pre-commit version pinned in workflows (`pip install pre-commit==x.y.z`).

description: Automerge non-major updates (minor, patch, pin, digest and lockFileMaintenance) once the required checks pass.

Renovate uses GitHub-native auto-merge (platformAutomerge defaults to true), so each repo's branch protection needs 'Allow auto-merge' enabled; where required reviews would block the merge, the renovate-approve app supplies the approval.
Repos can opt out per-dependency with: {"packageRules": [{"matchPackageNames": ["*"], "automerge": false}]}.

packageRules.description: Do not hold back our own Actions, reusable workflows and images: the cooldown is for third-party code, and our refs pinned to a branch (e.g. `@<sha> # main`) have no release timestamp, so the cooldown would block their digest updates forever.
Same for our own PyPI and npm packages, whose names lack the DIRACGrid/ prefix.
Group all GitHub Actions updates together.

Third-party Actions pinned to a branch (e.g. `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@<sha> # release/v1`) have no release timestamp, so with the default `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour` (timestamp-required) their digest updates would be held forever. Let them through; versioned refs (`# v4.2.0`) keep the cooldown.

description: Group all pre-commit hook updates together, instead of one PR per hook.

The explicit commitMessagePrefix makes the commit message deterministically conventional: Renovate's semantic prefixing is not reliably applied to grouped updates, which breaks repos that gate commits on a conventional-message check (e.g. DIRAC's semantic.yml).

packageRules.description: Lock file maintenance re-resolves everything to the newest version and skips minimumReleaseAge, so only the package manager can enforce a cooldown. pixi does it with `exclude-newer = "7d"` in pixi.toml / [tool.pixi.workspace] (set it in every pixi repo); npm has no rolling equivalent, so its lock files are not refreshed blindly.
Do not bump the CI interpreter (setup-python's python-version): it is pinned on purpose, e.g. 3.11 for old pre-commit hooks that break on Python 3.14.

Upper bounds in pyproject.toml are workarounds for known incompatibilities, so never raise them automatically. The updates are listed in the Dependency Dashboard, where a PR can be requested once the underlying problem is fixed.
